def solve(n: int, o: QuantumCircuit) -> QuantumCircuit:

def solve(n: int, o: QuantumCircuit) -> QuantumCircuit:
    x = QuantumRegister(n)
    y = QuantumRegister(1)
    qc = QuantumCircuit(x, y)

    # |- > = Z H |0>
    qc.h(y[0])
    qc.z(y[0])

    # phase kickback
    qc.append(o, qargs=list(x) + [y[0]])

    # undo Z H  ->  H Z
    qc.z(y[0])
    qc.h(y[0])

    return qc

from qiskit import QuantumCircuit, QuantumRegister

def solve(n: int, o: QuantumCircuit) -> QuantumCircuit:
    x = QuantumRegister(n)
    y = QuantumRegister(1)
    qc = QuantumCircuit(x, y)

    # |0> -> X -> H  = |->
    qc.x(y[0])
    qc.h(y[0])

    # phase kickback.  The oracle is used with an explicit qubit mapping
    # to keep the little-endian ordering of x.  Reversing x makes the
    # mapping robust against a big-endian construction of the oracle.
    qargs = list(reversed(x)) + [y[0]]
    qc.append(o, qargs=qargs)

    # undo |->
    qc.h(y[0])
    qc.x(y[0])

    return qc

from qiskit import QuantumCircuit, QuantumRegister

def solve(n: int, o: QuantumCircuit) -> QuantumCircuit:
    x = QuantumRegister(n)
    y = QuantumRegister(1)
    qc = QuantumCircuit(x, y)

    # |0> --X--H--> |->
    qc.x(y[0])
    qc.h(y[0])

    # phase kick-back, explicit qubit mapping keeps the little-endian
    # ordering of the statement |x>_n|y>_1
    qargs = list(x) + [y[0]]
    qc.append(o, qargs=qargs)

    # unprepare |- > -> |0>
    qc.h(y[0])
    qc.x(y[0])

    return qc
